newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX power futures driven higher near the close.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX power futures driven higher near the close.

text.p: NYMEX Palo Verde (PV) electricity futures settled higher in active trade near the close, while California-Oregon border (COB) contracts were little changed, market sources said Wednesday.
"A lot of people came in toward the end of the day. They wanted to run prices up," said one dealer.
Power futures opened higher amid stronger natural gas prices, but were back down by mid-day as gas prices fizzled.
However, the two energy markets "disconnected" in afternoon trading, as did futures prices and the over-the-counter market, said another trader.
"The best OTC bid for April PV was $13.65 (per megawatt hour), but I was buying it on the floor at $13.40," he noted.
Traders said a wide array of power plant outages continued to support prices, with continued delays in restarting the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant a major factor.
"The San Onofre unit is a (market) wild card," said one trader.
COB for April settled 6 cents higher at $9.65 per megawatt hour (MWh), while the May contract was up 5 cents at $9.75 and June was down 5 cents at $10.30.
PV for April closed 25 cents higher at $13.80, while May was up 15 cents at $14.10 and June was up 25 cents at $15.45.

In the Northwest, temperatures are forecast to average normal most of Thursday before cooling to two to four degrees F below normal Saturday. Storms bringing rain and mountain snow were expected to continue in the region tomorrow.
The Southwest was forecast to see dry and very warm weather before the weekend, with readings running four to eight degrees F above normal.
